topic: Section 1.8 — new H3 'Seasonal indeterminacy: the physical sun altitude swings 83%' (EXP-580 integration)
change_summary: EXP-580 integrated: new ~545-word H3 subsection inserted into Section 1.8 between 'A 1D function cannot solve a 3D problem' and 'What the refraction fix invalidates'. Restores the seasonal-altitude indeterminacy cascade (1,975–3,618 km) that was removed during a post-c3 rewrite. Closes ISS-2551 (WIN-046 stale cross-ref).
our_argument_summary: The new H3 argues that the dome's refraction fix — declaring the sun's 5,733 km apparent altitude an optical illusion — commits the physical sun to an altitude bounded above by H(r) = 8537·exp(−r/8619) km at the sun's seasonal orbital radius (Tropic of Cancer in June, Capricorn in December). Because H(r) is monotonically decreasing, the cap varies seasonally between ~1,975 km (December) and ~3,618 km (June) — an 83% swing relative to the lower bound. This forces a two-step squeeze on the medium n(r): either n(r) must lift the sun by different amounts each season (impossible — n(r) has no time dependence in the published model), or the physical sun must sit at the minimum cap year-round and n(r) must perform a factor-of-three lift that would simultaneously violate Gaia's 10-microarcsecond astrometry. The cascade then propagates to WIN-046 (S2 tide), WIN-056 (solar elevation), WIN-044 (FSF), and WIN-002/-029 (Schumann).

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r/8,619) km — the canonical dome ceiling function. Evaluated at three radii (June Tropic of Cancer, equator, December Tropic of Capricorn) drawn from AE-projection conventions consistent with the dome's coordinate conversion in 04-coordinates.txt. The refraction fix is verbatim from raw-text/05-model.txt line 38: 'Sun altitude (Observation): 5,733 km (optical illusion due to aetheric refraction)' with line 39 'Sun altitude (Physical): < 4,200 km (firmament limit).'

dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: The visible prose includes one hedge — 'What is contested is whether the model can absorb the consequence' — that gestures at the kernel of truth. The downstream cross-refs ('inherits the contradiction at one remove') use 'at one remove' as a deliberate hedge for the further-from-the-core links (Schumann, FSF) where the propagation is loose; see hole-2.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None at the model-parameter level. The dome's '<4,200 km' physical-sun bound is wider than the patch's seasonal bounds (1,975–3,618), so the patch is constraining the dome more tightly than the dome constrains itself — but the source of that tighter constraint is H(r) at the seasonal radius, which is the dome's own functional form applied at observed solstice positions. No mischaracterization of dome parameters.

quantitative_verification.notes: All claims reproduced to within rounding except the December bound, which sits at H(12600)=1978.86 in the bullet's frame and H(12614)=1975.62 in the AE-accurate frame. The patch's headline range '1,975 km (December) to 3,618 km (June)' is internally consistent only with the AE-accurate r=12,614; the bullet's r=12,600 yields ~1,979.

holes_found.description: Internal arithmetic inconsistency on the December bound. The bullet (data/sections.json: 'December solstice (Tropic of Capricorn, r = 12,600 km): H = 8,537 × exp(−1.462) ≈ 1,978 km') computes from r=12,600 km. Three lines later the prose's headline range cites '1,975 km (December) to 3,618 km (June)'. With strict r=12,600 km the consistent value is H≈1,978.86 km, not 1,975 km. The 1,975 km value corresponds to r≈12,617 km (the AE-projection-accurate Tropic of Capricorn at lat −23.4366°, which gives r = 10,008 × (90+23.4366)/90 = 12,614.15 km, H=1975.6). A hostile reader will see the bullet computing 1,978 and the headline using 1,975 and ask which number is the dome bound — it is also the input to the immediately-following '78% stronger refraction' figure (correct under either bound to two-sig-fig rounding, but quoted from the larger gap so the inconsistency carries forward). Patch then says 'physical sun must sit below ~1,975 km' as the bullet's own conclusion, three kilometres below the bullet's own computed value. The internal mismatch is small in magnitude (~3 km) but reputationally costly because the patch's own framing — 'The numbers above are computed directly from the dome's own functional form using the dome's own parameters: nothing here is contested arithmetic' — invites exactly this style of audit.
holes_found.recommendation: Pick one regime. Either: (a) update the bullet to r=12,614 km / H≈1,975 km (the AE-accurate Tropic of Capricorn radius, matching the headline range); or (b) update the headline range and 'physical sun must sit below' to '~1,979 km' to match the r=12,600 bullet. Option (a) is preferred because the AE-accurate radius is what the dome's own coordinate convention would give, and it leaves the visible 83% swing figure unchanged.

holes_found.description: WIN-002 / WIN-029 (Schumann) cross-ref in the final paragraph is structurally loose. WIN-002 and WIN-029 argue that the dome's H(r) ceiling, integrated over the disc, gives Schumann frequencies of ~22 Hz (or ~35 Hz area-weighted) rather than the observed 7.83 Hz — a contradiction with H(r)'s overall functional form, not with H(r)'s seasonal coupling to a moving sun. Schumann cavity resonance is a global, time-stationary property of the cavity geometry; the sun's seasonal track does not modulate it. The new H3 claims Schumann 'inherits the contradiction at one remove,' which is hedged enough to be technically defensible, but a dome defender will note that the seasonal-indeterminacy mechanism is genuinely orthogonal to the Schumann frequency mismatch — the two critiques live on the same H(r) function but operate by different mechanisms. The 'at one remove' hedge then reads as overclaim by association.
holes_found.recommendation: Either drop WIN-002/-029 from the final cascade paragraph (FSF/WIN-044 is enough to make the 'downstream of H(r)' point), or replace the cross-ref with a sharper formulation: 'WIN-002/-029 attack the same H(r) function from a different direction — the cavity-integrated frequency — making it the structurally most-loaded function in the model, not from the seasonal-indeterminacy angle.' The current 'inherits the contradiction at one remove' framing conflates two separate H(r) failures.

holes_found.description: WIN-056 framing in the cascade paragraph slightly mischaracterizes that WIN's central argument. The H3 says: 'Solar-elevation-from-H(r) predictions (WIN-056) face the constraint from the other direction: the very H(r) function that supplies a fixed-looking ceiling collapses into a seasonally swinging one when the sun is allowed to move.' But WIN-056's actual published argument (verdict Self-Contradicted) is that the dome's solar elevation formula uses the globe's 23.45° axial-tilt declination function (φ_sun(t) = 23.45° × sin(2π(t−81)/365)) — a globe formula — rather than deriving solar elevation from dome geometry (arctan(H_sun / d_observer)). WIN-056's primary mechanism is axial-tilt-formula misuse, not 'H(r) collapses into a seasonally swinging ceiling.' The seasonal-indeterminacy critique here is a NEW failure mode the cascade paragraph should claim adds to WIN-056, not a re-derivation of WIN-056's existing argument. (The EXP file's anticipated_objections #4 acknowledges WIN-056 'is the original anchor of the 5,733 km conflict' and tries to distinguish the new framing from WIN-056's existing one, but the visible prose's 'from the other direction' phrasing is not unambiguous about that distinction.)
holes_found.recommendation: Reframe the WIN-056 sentence to: 'Solar-elevation-from-H(r) predictions (WIN-056) — already self-contradicted by their reliance on the globe's 23.45° axial-tilt formula — gain a second contradiction when the H(r) ceiling that bounds the sun's physical altitude is itself seasonally swinging.' This preserves the cascade-inheritance claim without misrepresenting WIN-056's primary mechanism.

holes_found.description: Equinox H(r) value is rounded down by ~1 km. Bullet says 'r = 10,008 km, H = 8,537 × exp(−1.161) ≈ 2,672 km'. Independent computation: H(10008) = 8537·exp(-10008/8619) = 8537·exp(-1.161156) = 2673.14 km. Patch rounds to 2,672 instead of 2,673. Triviality — but in a paragraph whose rhetorical anchor is 'nothing here is contested arithmetic,' publication-quality rounding matters.
holes_found.recommendation: Update bullet to '≈ 2,673 km'. Single character change.

stronger_arguments.description: The two-step n(r) squeeze could close more tightly by noting that n(r) must ALSO satisfy the Polaris-observation constraint that anchors the dome's coordinate conversion (V12: r(city) = solve numerically: r · tan(θ_Polaris) = H(r)). That coordinate conversion already uses n(r) implicitly (per Section 1.8's earlier paragraph 'The coordinate system depends on the same medium'). So the same n(r) must now perform: (a) a season-dependent lift of the sun by 1,640 km of amplitude, (b) a 3.0× lift of the sun's apparent altitude over its physical altitude, (c) zero perturbation of Polaris's apparent zenith angle that the coordinate system reads as 'latitude', and (d) sub-microarcsecond perturbation of 1.8 billion Gaia stellar positions. The single-parameter n(r) cannot fit four orthogonal constraints. The current H3 makes the (a), (b), (d) case explicitly and leaves (c) implicit via the prior paragraph — making the cascade fully reach back to the section's opening would strengthen the seal.
sources: data/sections.json:section-1-8 paragraph on V12 coordinate conversion

stronger_arguments.description: The Gaia-precision quantitative claim could be sharpened. The H3 currently says n(r) doing the 3.0× lift 'would displace Gaia's 10-microarcsecond stellar positions by amounts many orders of magnitude' above precision. A back-of-envelope anchor: a refractive medium that bends light through 1,975 km of vertical altitude up to an apparent 5,733 km requires a deflection angle of roughly arctan((5733-1975)/d_observer); for a typical observer at d=5000 km this is ~37° of deflection. Stellar light passing through the same medium near zenith would suffer arcseconds (not microarcseconds) of deflection — five-to-six orders of magnitude above Gaia's 10-µas floor. Putting one quantitative anchor in the prose ('Gaia's measured precision is 10 µas; the lift required here implies stellar deflections in the arcsecond regime, five to six orders of magnitude larger') makes the empirical anchor unattackable.

kernel_of_truth.description: The H3 acknowledges one kernel implicitly: 'The numbers above are computed directly from the dome's own functional form using the dome's own parameters: nothing here is contested arithmetic. What is contested is whether the model can absorb the consequence.' This is the right kernel — the dome's H(r) function (EXP-580.json:patch_new paragraph 2) is mathematically determinate and the dome model's published value 5,733 km (raw-text/05-model.txt:38) is a real commitment, not a strawman. The new H3 does not claim H(r) itself is broken; it claims H(r) combined with the refraction fix and a seasonally moving sun forces an internal-consistency obligation the dome has not yet discharged. The EXP file's full kernel_of_truth statement is sharper than what reaches the visible prose, but the brevity is defensible in a 545-word insertion that the surrounding section already grounds in 'A medium 300–6,000× more refractive than Earth's atmosphere' (data/sections.json:section-1-8 summary tldr).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Mathematical determinacy of H(r) is necessary but not sufficient for prediction (EXP-580.json:why_kernel_doesnt_save_claim). The dome model needs H(r) plus a self-consistent physical interpretation of the sun's altitude that survives the sun's seasonal motion (data/wins.json:WIN-056 verdict 'Self-Contradicted' shows the existing seasonal-handling already relies on the globe's axial-tilt formula). The new H3 (data/sections.json:section-1-8) closes one degree of freedom the dome could have used to escape: by tying physical-altitude variability to H(r) evaluated at observed-fact seasonal radii, the patch forces n(r) into a role it cannot fill — either time-dependent (impossible by published functional form) or factor-of-three at one fixed altitude (incompatible with Gaia astrometry per anticipated_objections #2). The kernel survives intact; the model does not.

text_fingerprint.h3_title: Seasonal indeterminacy: the physical sun altitude swings 83%

deeper_analysis: The new H3 is a genuine strengthening of Section 1.8. The Section 1.8 narrative before this insertion already argued (i) the refraction fix declaring 5,733 km an optical illusion implicates the coordinate system because Polaris light traverses the same medium, and (ii) the medium would have to be 300–6,000× more refractive than Earth's atmosphere. The new H3 inserts a third argument: even if (i) and (ii) could be patched, the refraction fix commits the physical sun to an altitude bounded by H(r) at the seasonal orbital radius, and H(r) varies enough across the sun's seasonal track to force an internal contradiction on n(r). This is not double-counting (i) or (ii) — it's a new closure that operates on time-domain seasonal motion rather than spatial-domain coordinate calibration. The two-step n(r) squeeze (time-dependence-required or factor-of-3-required-with-Gaia-violation) is the load-bearing structural move and it is sound. The four anticipated_objections in the EXP file are well-targeted at the strongest defender positions (free-parameter seasonal-amplitude function, fixed-min-altitude with constant n(r) lift, 83%-as-rhetorical-inflation, WIN-056 double-counting) and each response holds. The hole that matters in the visible prose is the 1,975 vs 1,978 internal mismatch on the December bound — every other concern is minor framing or cross-ref tightening. Net assessment: deep-attack review confirms the new content earns its place in Section 1.8; recommend minor_edit to fix the December-bound arithmetic mismatch and tighten the Schumann/WIN-056 cross-refs. No verdict change is at stake because the target is a section, not a WIN.
advocate_mode: Steelman: the dome's best response is anticipated_objections #2 — 'physical sun at 1,975 km year-round, n(r) lifts to 5,733 in every season.' This DOES preserve consistency with H(r) everywhere on the orbital track (since H(r) ≥ 1,978 for all r ≤ 12,600). The EXP closes this defense by chaining it to Gaia astrometry: the same n(r) that lifts a 1,975 km sun to apparent 5,733 km cannot leave 1.8 billion stellar positions undisplaced at 10-µas precision. The closure depends on n(r) having no wavelength dependence in the published functional form — which is true; raw-text/05-model.txt presents n(r) as a scalar field with no λ argument. The Gaia precision anchor is the load-bearing empirical fact; the patch could anchor it more explicitly with a deflection-angle estimate (see stronger_arguments above) but the qualitative claim survives even without that. Steelman-defense conclusion: dome has no published escape from the closure; an unpublished escape via n(r,λ,t) is a free-parameter rescue and exits the model's current parameter set.
cross_win_consistency: Cross-refs to WIN-046, WIN-056, WIN-044, WIN-002, WIN-029 examined against current wins.json verdicts: all five carry verdict 'Self-Contradicted' as of HEAD b2d0972, so the cascade-inheritance framing is consistent with the model's overall standing on these targets. WIN-044 (FSF) already cross-references Section 1.8 ('A second structural contradiction is documented in Section 1.8') in its detail_evidence, so the inbound link from this new H3 to WIN-044 closes a loop. WIN-046 (S2 tidal) cross-ref is the original justification for this EXP (closes ISS-2551 stale-cross-ref). WIN-056 framing is loose (hole 3). WIN-002/-029 framing is loose (hole 2). Cross-WIN consistency is otherwise clean.

summary_for_decider: EXP-580 deep-attack review (qid=471). New H3 in Section 1.8 is a sound strengthening of the section. One MODERATE hole: internal arithmetic inconsistency on the December bound — bullet uses r=12,600 / H=1,978 km but headline immediately quotes '1,975 km (December)' and 'physical sun must sit below ~1,975 km.' The 1,975 km value is consistent with the AE-accurate Tropic of Capricorn radius r=12,614 km, but inconsistent with the patch's stated r=12,600. Recommend single-line fix: change bullet to 'r = 12,614 km' and recompute display value to '≈ 1,975 km' (option a, preferred), OR update headline + below-bound to '~1,979 km' (option b). Four minor holes: WIN-002/-029 Schumann cross-ref is overclaim by association (Schumann inherits H(r) form but not the seasonal mechanism), WIN-056 framing is imprecise (WIN-056 attacks axial-tilt formula, not H(r) ceiling collapse), equinox H rounded down by 1 km (2,672 vs 2,673), 5,733 km 'held suspiciously fixed' could cite raw-text/05-model.txt:38 directly. ISS-2551 closure is appropriate. No verdict change. No carry-over from prior cycles. Confidence 0.85. Recommended action: minor_edit. Two stronger-argument suggestions: (i) close the n(r) cascade back to Polaris/coordinate-system constraint already in the section opener, making the n(r) squeeze four-way rather than two-way; (ii) anchor the Gaia 'many orders of magnitude' claim on a deflection-angle estimate (arcsec regime vs Gaia's 10 µas floor) — turns a qualitative anchor into a 5–6 OOM quantitative one. Both are polish, not blockers.
